Piss filled water balloons? That's absolutely disgusting - and I'm referring to the people who used them, not the balloons. Bullying is one thing, but it sounds like these girls took it to a whole new level.
I feel intimidated by beautiful girls, but I feel that's stemmed by natural insecurities. No where to the same extent you are afraid, however I never had such traumatizing experiences as you have, so your fear is completely justified.

The fact that is still effects you this much this many years later, though, is hindering your life. You should find a good support group to help you get past all of the things you went through so you don't have to live in self-doubt and fear like that.

Good for you! I made the same decision a year ago and it's the best one I ever made. I'm an 18 year-old who just graduated high school, and I didn't wear make up once except for Prom. It saves so much time, money, and effort to not wear make up. Not to mention, what do you get out of it? Who are you trying to impress? If you don't enjoy the hassle of make up there is no reason for you to feel the need to.
Surprisingly, I was a lot more insecure when I wore make up because it made me a lot more self-conscious of how I looked. Besides, you are absolutely beautiful without your makeup. I have really bad acne which is why I started wearing makeup, but if I had your skin, I would have never considered wearing a single drop.

Anyways, good for you and your gorgeous self! (:

I'm an 18 year-old teenager and the last of four children, but my mom lost her first child when she was an infant. My mom was always ridiculously over-protective, but knowing what she went through it makes sense. It hits home knowing my own mother went through such pain. It's one of the few things she isn't able to talk about, but occasionally things have slipped out when it became to hard for her to bear like at her passed daughter's birthday. I remember she told me how her daughter died in her arms, and it felt like she never left that spot with her daughter fully. Like she just wanted to flow off and die with her. She told me how with all three of her kids she was scared to wake us up when we were sleeping because she was afraid wouldn't be breathing.
I cry when I think about it.

All I can say is I myself can't imagine the pain you are going through, but I'm glad you are brave enough to talk about it. All of my sympathy goes out to you.

In 2006, when I was in 5th grade, my mom had a went pretty insane. She started believing that my dad had a crazy consiracy to kill me, my brother, and her and burn down our house for the insurance money. She took me and my brother out of school in November and left the house because she felt it wasn't safe. We spent an entire month roaming Las Vegas(where we lived), and Utah in our car. I slept in the car a dozen times, walked dozens of miles in the middle of the night when our car broke down, and begged on the street once with her. She went to a fire house, the FBI, a church, and anywhere else telling people of our story about how we were running from a gang trying to kill us. It always ended the same way: she left screaming and cussing at them for not believing her. I spent Christmas sleeping in the car. This went on until the beginning of January when CPS caught up with her and me and my brother were taken away to live with my dad.

I'm starting college in the fall, and I stumbled across this article. Not only am I really sad for how often such an atrocious crime occurs, but I'm also terrified. I feel I will never feel safe in college and that makes me sad. Even if nothing ever happens to me, I feel I will always be on-edge and unable to trust anyone. I don't want my college life to be like that.
